title: An atlas of widow spiders (Araneae: Theridiidae: Latrodectus Walckenaer, 1805): phylogeny, biogeography, and integrated taxonomy
content:
Abstract
Widow spiders (genus Latrodectus) have remarkable biology and an infamous reputation. They are known for their neurotoxic venom and warning coloration. Behavioural and morphological aspects of their dramatic sexual biology make them productive study subjects. Understanding the evolution of these phenomena requires a rigorous phylogenetic hypothesis and an applicable system for how the various species involved are circumscribed. However, the taxonomy of Latrodectus has proved especially challenging and has suffered from critical errors and misinterpretations. We take an integrated approach to advancing the systematics of widow spiders, complementing a molecular phylogeny with the examination of key type specimens and photodocumentation of voucher specimens. Where possible, sequence data were obtained from specimens from near type localities to provide exemplars representing particular species concepts. We present a time-calibrated global-scope multilocus phylogenetic study of widow spiders and revise species limits and synonymies in light of those results. The resulting biogeographical pattern indicates an Afroeurasian origin, with independent radiations in North America, South America, and Australasia, plus a secondary movement from the North American clade into northern South America. We recognize 39 valid Latrodectus species plus one more awaiting description; three previously valid species are formally synonymized, and seven species are revalidated.
